methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $13M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Sarla Aviation is a Series A transportation company founded by Rakesh Gaonkar and Adrian Schmidt, having raised $13M to date. The broader transportation sector comprises eight private comparables including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Pipedream, and FleetZero, with no public peers directly comparable at this stage and valuation tier.

A single valuation method proved applicable. The Stage-Progression approach uses the $13M total raised as a proxy for current post-money valuation and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $26M. Peer-Median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow transportation peer set—while three transportation companies exist in the broader comp universe, none met filtering thresholds (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier) required to support reliable median pricing.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $22M (low) to $30M (high), with a median point of $26M. This range reflects the single-method constraint; triangulation confidence is limited by reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than market multiples. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for Sarla's specific subsector dynamics and the lack of direct peer benchmarking. Additional diligence on unit economics, capital efficiency, and market size relative to named comparables would strengthen conviction.
